result.summary: A bounded, zero-experiment, zero-network, non-batch internal algebraic-derivation task attempting to construct an explicit compact pairwise object for decks 2 and 3 of H-CREP-001's frozen P1553 instance model, analogous to load_pair_product_generators for decks 0-1, and a combination rule merging it with the existing decks-0/1 generators while staying reduced modulo g_I throughout. Unlike TASK-20260830-e30c67 (which found zero decomposition attempts anywhere in the frozen record), this session actually constructed a candidate: two purely local pairwise generator objects (G01_local, G23_local, built by an admissibility test using only the two paired occurrences' own fields, with no peek at other decks) plus a deck-4 admissible-label lookup, combined via a set intersection for support (V4) and a Cartesian product for exact tuple replay (V5). This candidate was hand-verified, field for field, against six of the twelve recorded instances (four by full numeric trace spanning single_hit, repeated_source at both B=2 and B=3, and no_relation_unit; two by direct structural argument), exactly reproducing every reference support set and replay tuple list checked, at additive existence cost and empirically-additive replay cost within all H-CREP-001 preprocessing/online caps. A degenerate-case check found the replay step's true shape is a bounded Cartesian product, not a structurally additive one, and would blow up combinatorially under multiplicities the frozen 12-instance family never exercises. The candidate cannot be discharged as a gate-passing trigger for two independent, named reasons: a fully certain procedural fact (it requires node kinds absent from check_representation.py's frozen PREPROCESSING_KINDS/ONLINE_KINDS vocabulary, and adding them would be an out-of-scope EXP-CREP-001 specification change), and a directly-checkable but explicitly non-airtight substantive argument (its correctness mechanism implies a natural construction degree of O(B), while r_R is declared to have degree Theta(B^2), a mismatch that depends on which of two named, unconfirmed explanations for that stated degree is correct -- disclosed as an open uncertainty, not resolved). This was checked against docs/inventor-protocol.md Section 8's four audits including a proves-too-much control against the same classical subproduct-tree/known-linear-factors nearby object used in both prior rounds, on directly-stated-quantity grounds rather than the definitional assertion the earlier gate-framing-review round was found to rest on. Disposition is recorded as obstruction_extended, explicitly scoped to transfer/gate-discharge of this one constructed candidate, not to toy-level constructibility (which this session answers affirmatively, closing that specific sub-question of KN-OPEN-7f424d) and not to a general impossibility claim about decks-2-4 decomposition (explicitly not made). Of the prior round's five proof obligations: correctness and interface/target-independence are discharged for the toy model; runtime is discharged with a named multiplicity caveat for the toy model; feasibility is partially discharged (toy yes, real not established); toy-to-real transfer scope is addressed with a new, named, though disclosed-as-uncertain, negative argument rather than left untouched.
